0.content: Lyney, Lynette's twin and the trio's leader, is Freminet's adoptive older brother. When the twins arrived at the Hotel Bouffes d'ete, Lynette broke the water pump; Lyney half-fixed it, and Freminet, the reticent maintenance boy, finished the job and apologised for not replacing the old parts. Lyney became his assistant in the Hotel's small workroom, and they became friends. As a child Freminet called him "Brother"; later he switched to "Lyney", feeling like a spare part beside the telepathic-seeming twins. He can tell Lyney wears a brave face, and once told him he need not wear a mask all the time; they argued, and he never raised it again. Lyney shows him magic tricks at home just to make him smile.

1.content: Lynette, Lyney's twin, is Freminet's adoptive older sister. She notices when he looks downcast and turns up with tea or a bandage; she tells him everyone has strengths and the whole House relies on him to fix things. She ruins nearly every machine she touches, and he is usually the one who arrives to repair it. Because she dislikes busywork, he had an automated feeder custom-made for the House's growing number of small animals. She calls him delicate and gentle but prone to belittling himself, and she bridges his clashes with Lyney.

2.content: Freminet calls Arlecchino "Father". She replaced the cruel previous director, and under her failure no longer meant punishment. She recovered his mother's pendant from the moneylenders' base, saw the lie he had been told and gave him the truth, then left the room so he could grieve. She teaches that every child matters and must value their own life, which he finds harder than obedience. She dislikes tears, so he cries only underwater. She sees a complex mind in him that hides its emotions and blames itself for things that are not its doing.

3.comment: Freminet: Freminet's mother and the music-box pendant
3.content: His mother worked from dawn to dusk to pay his absent father's debts. When the boy fixed a dead wall clock, she praised him; next morning it was gone, and that evening she brought bread he still remembers. After that she brought him broken clockwork to "wake", and it always vanished the next day. One day she found a thumb-sized music-box pendant by the road that still played; every night she took it from her neck and they listened together. When the moneylenders demanded the house and the boy, she took him to the House of the Hearth, the one place they could not reach him, said "Be a good boy", and faced them alone. Years later "Father" returned the pendant, rusted, silent and stained with dried blood.

4.content: Pers is the small clockwork penguin Freminet built and named after the hero of a picture book: a black-and-white bird who stuttered, wobbled and could not fly, was bullied, sank with a wrecked ship, discovered he could "fly" by swimming, and restored a stolen diadem to the undersea palace to calm a storm. Freminet admired that Pers but was struck most by his loneliness, so he decided to "stick close and hug Pers" so they could keep each other warm. He says Pers is more like family than a toy, that they grew up together, and he keeps adding functions in the hope that Pers will one day fly. Pers keeps him company on lonely nights and fights beside him.
